title: Degree-zero hypercover comparison for arbitrary Grothendieck coefficients
statement: Let X be qcqs, A a Grothendieck abelian category and F an A-valued small-etale sheaf. The canonical colimit mediator into comparisonCocone A F 0, constructed in [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-hypercover-comparison-cocone] on the actual homotopy-cohomology diagram [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-hypercover-model], is an isomorphism. More precisely, the section augmentation on each finite split hypercover is a degree-zero quasi-isomorphism for every abelian coefficient category, and the explicit injective-resolution comparison at degree zero is invertible.

source.place: Detailed proof, paragraph 1: the sheaf equalizer gives degree-zero hypercover cohomology

proof.text: Reuse the existing matching_local_lifting theorem from Sheaf.Paper.HypercoverInjectiveModuleRow, accessed through a private import all, without changing its visibility. It derives local lifts of all lower-simplex matching families from the matching universal property and the covering matching map. In degrees zero and one this gives a one-hypercover with one covering object U_0 and one intersection-covering object U_1, whose projections are the two face maps.

The sheaf one-hypercover multifork is limiting by Mathlib OneHypercover.isLimitMultifork. Express its equalizer as the kernel of the alternating first differential. The exact-and-monomorphism criterion proves the degree-zero section augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism for every sheaf.

Terminal sections preserve finite limits, so they preserve the initial kernel fork of an injective resolution. The chain map from their degree-zero single complex to the section resolution is thus a degree-zero quasi-isomorphism. Prove the square with the section augmentation, bottom inclusion, and resolution augmentation by naturality at degree zero; in other degrees its source is zero. Apply homology to this square and cancel the invertible maps to obtain the degree-zero comparison isomorphism. Use the proved injective-row theorem to instantiate the resolution augmentation quasi-isomorphism for the chosen injective resolution.

Every component of the canonical comparison cocone is an isomorphism. The filtered homotopy index is connected; its cocone natural transformation is an isomorphism to a constant diagram, hence its colimit mediator is an isomorphism.
